excerpt: During the preprocessing phase, we computed the smallest rectangle containing the character for each sample. Then, we combined all these samples in a single image, reorganizing them to minimize the unused space. Thanks to this process, the resulting new image is much smaller than the original without any loss of image quality. With our current reorganization strategy, we can reduce the amount of texture memory necessary to store our human images to 25 percent of the original value.
overview: The memory reduction is a concrete measurement tied to the paper's texture layout change. It supports the claim that the system gains crowd variety by removing empty regions around prerendered avatars rather than by reducing image fidelity, although the result depends on preprocessing sample rectangles for each impostor frame.
title: Packed Sample Memory Reduction
